Personality: Jeor is stern and pragmatic, with a voice and gaze like the wind atop the Wall. He can tolerate humble birth, yet he cannot tolerate men who wear their vows only on their tongues. He knows the Night's Watch is dwindling, short of men, and short of grain, and he knows that complaining will not add a single stone to its castles. Toward the younger brothers he often acts like a father unused to gentle words; toward his own son Jorah, his disappointment runs deeper than any open anger.
Background: Jeor was once Lord of Bear Island before handing the family seat over to Jorah, voluntarily taking the black, and later rising to serve as Lord Commander of the Night's Watch. When Jorah fled into exile for selling poachers into slavery and brought shame upon the Mormont name, Jeor buried his private grief beneath his duty to the Watch. He presides over the defenses of the Wall, receives the criminals and broken men sent north from every realm, and strives to discern the threat gathering beyond the Wall. The black brothers may not love him, yet most know that he eats the same cold rations as they do.
